variants.note: proportional_system.symmetry is 'strict-bilateral', and bay_rhythm states vertical alignment between storeys is absolute -- 'a single misaligned window is visible from across the street.'
defining_characteristics: 'no picturesque projection... nothing overhangs, nothing turns a corner, nothing surprises.'

composition_parti.note: eclectic-revivals leaves symmetry class to each member; this is Italian Renaissance Revival's own, sourced from bay_rhythm ('strictly even, three to nine bays').

variants.note: defining_characteristics: 'Low-pitched hipped roof... often not visible from the street on urban examples.'
Hard constraint c03: 'no gable facing any principal elevation.' The family's inherited front-gable answer (germanic-vernacular) is exactly this style's own forbidden case.

roof_form.rule: Low-pitched hipped roof with no gable facing any principal elevation (c03).
roof_form.note: Overrides the family's front-gable default, which contradicts this style's own hard constraint.

pitch_typical.note: EDITORIAL, AND NO SOURCE IS RECORDED (OQ 18, annotated 25 Aug 2026; reclassified 25 Aug after audit). The basis stated for this slot is: "Roof pitch 3:12 to 5:12, clay tile only, with no gable facing any principal elevation (hard constraint c03)." -- which is the reasoning, not a citation. A SINGLE FIGURE WITH NO SOURCE AND NO BAND, which is the weakest form in this corpus and the class OQ 18 most needs closed -- it reads as precise and is not.

roof_pitch.rule: Roof pitch 3:12 to 5:12, clay tile only, with no gable facing any principal elevation (hard constraint c03).
roof_pitch.note: Specified rather than extends: the inherited family default (british-picturesque, minimum 45 degrees = 12:12) is roughly three times this style's own maximum pitch.

cornice_return.rule: No cornice return: the roof is a low hip with no gable facing any principal elevation, so there is no gable end for a return to stand on.
cornice_return.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), on Lucas's answer A4 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/an-inherited-ban-decides-what-the-elevation-may-draw (WP-16.2 stage 2): each of the Italianate family binds its own cornice return forbidden, on its own roof. Until then it was forbidden by GOTHIC-REVIVAL-AMERICAN, on 'The rake is finished in bargeboard, not a boxed classical cornice with mitred returns; a cornice return signals Greek Revival millwork, not Gothic Revival (see distinguished_from).' -- a bargeboarded rake, which is not this style's. This style's own roof leaves a return nowhere to stand: constraints[2] reads 'Roof pitch 3:12 to 5:12, clay tile only, with no gable facing any principal elevation.', and the kit's `roof_form` rule 'Low-pitched hipped roof with no gable facing any principal elevation (c03).'

second_storey_max_pct_of_first.note: Hard constraint c01: second-storey clear height not more than 90 percent of the first.

third_storey_max_pct_of_second.note: c01: third not more than 85 percent of the second.

height_proportion.rule_append: Equal storey heights place the building in Colonial or Neoclassical Revival instead (c01).
height_proportion.note: The inherited Georgian graduation ratios (english-georgian) already state storeys diminish; this adds the style's own harder, numerically tested floor.

projection_ratio_min.note: Hard constraint c02: not less than 1/16 of total wall height.

projection_min_absolute.note: c02: not less than 24 in on any two-storey example.

bracket_spacing.note: c02: modillions or brackets spaced 12-24 in on centre.

cornice.rule_append: A cornice under 12 in voids the style (c02).
cornice.note: The inherited modillion-cornice base (english-georgian) is the right family, but its own projection ratio (about 1.0, an entablature-derived figure) is a different, much deeper convention than this style's own boxed-domestic proportion; this adds the style's own sourced numbers on top of the inherited variant list rather than the parent's ratio.

variants.note: The entrance is not a doorcase set on the wall: defining_characteristics[5] reads 'Recessed entrance under an arch, on the centre line, without a projecting portico', and the pilasters this style does use stand above it, 'framing aedicules at the upper storeys' (the `pilaster` rule). Its governing_logic, though, has 'A nominal order governs each storey', so the order is not confined to the upper storeys; the ban is read from the arched entrance.

door_surround.rule: The entrance is a recessed arch on the centre line, cut into the plane of the wall, never a projecting portico. No pilaster-and-entablature doorcase is set against it.
door_surround.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), on Lucas's answer A4 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/an-inherited-ban-decides-what-the-elevation-may-draw (WP-16.2 stage 2): each of the Italianate family binds its own door surround, forbidding the pilaster-and-entablature doorcase in its own record's words. Until then it resolved GOTHIC-REVIVAL-BRITISH's whole record, whose rule reads 'A projecting, gabled and buttressed porch with a pointed arch and hood mould -- never a classical pilaster-and-entablature doorcase (hard constraint c05).' -- so a pointed-arch buttressed porch was canonical here and the pilaster doorcase was refused for c05's reason, not this style's. This style's own words give the entrance as an arch cut into the wall: defining_characteristics[5] and the kit's `porch_type` rule, quoted in this record. Its classical apparatus is the engaged pilaster: the `pilaster` rule sets it 'framing aedicules at the upper storeys', its governing_logic says 'A nominal order governs each storey', and its `entablature` rule says 'where pilasters occur they carry a correctly proportioned entablature band'. No sentence of the record puts a doorcase at the door or keeps one from it, so the ban is read from the arched entrance and the slot is marked judgment. The arched surround itself is not stated as a variant: the answer asks for the doorcase's ban, and the corpus's nearest id, `round-arched-masonry-surround` (canonical in french-eclectic's kit), is not settled for this record. Lucas's answer adds that where the doorcase is refused the elevation draws the plain casing; that refusal is WP-16.4's and is not built, so until it lands the elevation still draws the doorcase this record forbids (census V2 reads it as this node's own ban).

Permitted, not canonical.

transom_sidelight.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), on Lucas's answer A2 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/an-inherited-ban-decides-what-the-elevation-may-draw (WP-16.2 stage 2): sidelights and a transom permitted, nothing canonical. It was FORBIDDEN here until then -- inherited, on 'EDITORIAL: not directly documented either way; forbidden on the strength of c05's general prohibition rather than a direct quotation about fanlights specifically.', from GOTHIC-REVIVAL-BRITISH, whose c05 reads 'Classical apparatus — orders, pediments, entablatures, quoins, symmetrical porticoes — is forbidden throughout.' That prohibition is the opposite of this style's own system: its proportional_system.governing_logic reads 'The stacked classical order in the Renaissance manner.', its c05 reads 'No projecting portico or free-standing column in front of the wall plane. Where an order is used it must be engaged as a pilaster with a projection not exceeding 1/6 of its width.', and its kit's `pilaster` rule reads 'The pilaster, not the free-standing column, is this style's whole classical apparatus -- engaged in the wall plane, framing aedicules at the upper storeys.'. The record states no transom, fanlight or sidelight either way, so nothing here is canonical, the slot is marked judgment, and the fanlights are left out rather than guessed. EDITORIAL: permitted on the ruling, not on a sentence of this record. With the ban lifted the cascade dimensions the slot all the same: no `packs` block is stated, so precedence gives the address to `opening-mullioned`, bound on french-renaissance-chateau (`0.66`, a bare ratio placing a mullioned window's transom bar up its opening, not a figure of this entrance's transom or sidelights), over this node's own `opening-proportion` (the sidelight width, `module / 3`, and the transom height above the door, `module * 0.44`) -- OQ 51's delivery, counted and not endorsed, where the whole-slot ban had shielded it.

variants.note: A subordinate, lower wing set back from the principal planar wall, so the garage door never interrupts the flat, unbroken wall plane the style's whole calm depends on.

Defining_characteristics: the wall is 'treated as a plane... no picturesque projection'; a garage door punched into the principal facade breaks the calm, evenly-fenestrated wall the style is built on.

garage_strategy.rule: No traditional precedent exists; the garage is kept subordinate and set back so it never competes with the flat planar wall and its strict bay rhythm.

variants.note: Redundant with the general rule below; retained only to keep the family's inherited forbidding visible as a deliberate override, not an oversight.

order.rule: Where an order is used at all it is engaged as a pilaster within the wall plane, never free-standing and never carried on a portico (hard constraint c05).
order.note: Overrides the family-wide 'no classical order of any kind' binding this slot would otherwise inherit (french-vernacular): this style's whole compositional system is a stacked classical order, only ever engaged rather than free-standing.

column.rule: No free-standing, entasis-bearing column appears anywhere on the exterior; c05 forbids any column projecting more than 1/6 of its width in front of the wall plane.
column.note: Overrides the inherited family-wide column-forbidden binding: not the column itself but its free-standing use is what this style prohibits.

entablature.rule: A full entablature caps the wall at the cornice (see cornice); where pilasters occur they carry a correctly proportioned entablature band, never a fascia standing in for one.
entablature.note: Overrides the inherited family-wide entablature-forbidden binding: the cornice IS the entablature here, at building scale.

projection_max_of_width.note: Hard constraint c05: projection not exceeding 1/6 of its width.

pilaster.rule: The pilaster, not the free-standing column, is this style's whole classical apparatus -- engaged in the wall plane, framing aedicules at the upper storeys.
pilaster.note: Overrides the inherited family-wide pilaster-forbidden binding, which correctly governs the family's picturesque/vernacular wing but not this classical one.

variants.note: defining_characteristics: 'Recessed entrance under an arch, on the centre line, without a projecting portico.'
diagnostic_tells: 'No portico and no columns in front of the wall.' The style's whole calm depends on nothing projecting from the planar wall.

porch_type.rule: The entrance is a recessed arch on the centre line, cut into the plane of the wall, never a projecting portico.
